title: Multi-Agent Systems
description: Learn how to orchestrate multiple AI agents in a collaborative pipeline to plan, implement, and review code features.
learning_objectives: Define distinct roles and personas for specialized AI agents
Design a sequential hand-off workflow between a Planner and an Implementer
Implement an automated feedback loop for code review and refinement
Configure structured communication protocols to ensure reliable data transfer between agents

sections.heading: The Multi-Agent Architecture
sections.content_brief: Explain the concept of 'separation of concerns' in AI agents. Contrast a single monolithic prompt with a multi-agent system where specialized roles reduce hallucination and increase precision.

sections.heading: Defining Agent Personas
sections.content_brief: Detail how to write system prompts for two specific roles: the Technical Architect (Planner) and the Software Engineer (Implementer). Focus on defining clear boundaries, goals, and expected output formats for each.
sections.code_context: System prompt templates for a Planner agent and an Implementer agent

sections.heading: Building the Collaborative Pipeline
sections.content_brief: Demonstrate the technical implementation of a sequential pipeline. Show how to pass the output of the Planner (e.g., a technical spec) as the primary context for the Implementer's prompt.
sections.code_context: A Python script orchestrating two LLM calls where the second depends on the first

sections.heading: Implementing the Review Loop
sections.content_brief: Introduce a third agent or a feedback mechanism where the Planner reviews the Implementer's code against the original spec. Explain how to implement a conditional loop that triggers re-implementation if the review fails.
sections.code_context: A while-loop implementation that iterates between Implementation and Review agents until a 'PASS' signal is received

admonitions.content: Be careful to implement a maximum iteration limit (e.g., 3-5 loops) to prevent 'infinite loops' where agents disagree indefinitely, which can rapidly deplete your API credits.
Use structured formats like JSON or Markdown headers for agent hand-offs. This makes it significantly easier for the subsequent agent to parse specific requirements without noise.
